_comment: window_literals are the printable strings found in a fixed byte window around the env-block anchor; their job is to catch NEW fields cc adds near it. required_literals maps each field template this hook reimplements, but that window_literals cannot see at all, to its whole-binary occurrence count at pin time; Task 6 reports any CHANGE IN THAT COUNT rather than mere presence, which is what makes a rename or removal scoped to just ydE/_dE/vdE visible even though the string survives elsewhere in the binary. Counts, not a presence check or a floor, and deliberately: cc bumps its version on every release, so the version field above already fires on any upgrade, and these counts exist to tell a human reading that failure WHAT MOVED, not to gate a binary pass/fail — a count that drifted for an unrelated reason is a sentence in that report, not a false alarm to suppress. The split from window_literals exists because Kml()'s literals (behind the Shell: field) live in a different region of the binary's string table than the anchor's window, at any window size, not merely outside the current window's edges. Do not expect these counts to match a naive count of source occurrences: the binary embeds the app's compiled code twice (a serialized string-table copy and a separate readable-JS-source-text copy), so expect roughly double the naive per-function count before any other reuse; 'Platform: ' occurs in exactly 3 functions (ydE, _dE, vdE) yet its whole-binary count is 14, not 6, because three unrelated diagnostic/telemetry templates elsewhere in the binary also use the same short label — seeing 14 for a 3-occurrence field is correct, not a bug to round down. 'Shell: PowerShell' has none of that noise: all 3 whole-binary hits are Kml()'s own text (its Windows branch), which is why it stands in for the bare 7-char 'Shell: ' prefix — too short for window_literals's regex and, like Platform:, indistinguishable from unrelated uses if checked directly. Do not fold required_literals back into window_literals.
